newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian govt wins student budget measure.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian govt wins student budget measure.

text.p: Minority parties in the Australian Senate on Thursday tried and failed to block a budget measure tightening eligibility for student income support.

Key independent senator Mal Colston backed the Liberal-National government when the Labor, Democrat and Greens minority parties united in an attempt to disallow the regulation that put the measure into effect.
The other independent, Brian Harradine, voted with the minority parties, but his doing so resulted in only a tied vote -- not enough to carry the motion to disallow the regulation.
The measure becomes the second significant but doubtful budget measure to definitely survive the Senate, the other being a hike in student university charges that was passed last week.
However, the government was foreced to dilute the measure to gain Senate passage, widening eligibility for student support a little at a cost of A$9 million a year.
A government official estimated that the measure as passed was worth about A$54 million in 1997/98, its first full year of operation, and A$69 million in 1999/00.

Most contentious budget measures are implemented by an act of parliament. This one, and a few others, were implemented by regulation -- effectively, a ministerial order -- that either house of parliament can disallow.
About a quarter of the budget's A$7.2 billion 1997/98 fiscal tightening is at risk in the Senate.
